imperātīvus, imperātīva, imperātīvum

Declension on Wiktionary

imperative; as a noun (modus understood), the imperative

modus imperātīvus, the imperative mood: lege!, legite! (Traupman 229). To form the imperative of a verb is facere imperātīvum (Traupman 246). We have found no classical name for it; Quintilian contrasts nē and nōn as vetandī and negandī, of forbidding and of denying (1.5.50).

Examples

  • Dīc imperātīvum modum ejusdem verbī, tempore praesentī, singulāriter et plūrāliter.

    Give the present imperative of the same verb in the singular and the plural.Traupman 229

See also mood, indicative, subjunctive, grammar.
